description: One admitted source entails one conclusion.
A conclusion of the first rule is the second rule's premise.
Two independent properties of one subject jointly establish review.
A three-way join requires all three independently admitted facts.
The account on the transfer must be the same account with a flag.
Three ancestor links yield a recursive transitive conclusion.
A supplied symmetric relation permits reversing a known relation.
Two edges entail a transitive edge, with no equality shortcut.
Explicit type and class relation derive a wider type.
The inverse rule preserves subject/object identity.
A predicate variable is bound consistently in a two-body rule.
A self relation satisfies the repeated-variable pattern.
A fully ground rule head is allowed under the supplied rule.
A bound source object may appear in the conclusion.
Duplicate source facts retain two claims but one logical triple.
Either of two proof paths may establish the same goal.
An unrelated admitted source must not change the result.
An inapplicable rule must not manufacture an unrelated conclusion.
A fully ground premise and conclusion can be checked.
An exact admitted goal needs no inference step.
A seeded positive cycle can derive the other state.
An asserted goal stays established when a rule points back to itself.
Circular rules alone establish neither member.
A two-premise rule cannot fire with only one premise.
Facts about different accounts do not satisfy one joined variable.
An edge does not entail its reverse without a rule.
Two unequal terms cannot satisfy a repeated variable.
A valid rule about another predicate does not prove the requested goal.
No facts and a positive rule do not establish the goal.
The chain stops before the requested final state.
Target expired before the evaluation time.
valid_until is exclusive at the exact evaluation instant.
One second before expiry is within the target validity window.
Target's validity window has not begun.
valid_from is inclusive at the exact evaluation instant.
A target for another repository is inapplicable.
A production target does not apply to test.
Absent required repository context admits neither source nor target.
Absent required environment context admits neither source nor target.
A host request cannot borrow a model-only target.
A host+model request requires both audiences on every used claim.
Matching host+model labels satisfy the applicability contract.
An expired premise is excluded before proof generation.
A future premise is excluded before proof generation.
A premise from another repository cannot support this goal.
A premise from another environment cannot support this goal.
Authored approved text without a receipt is not a premise.
Changed source bytes invalidate the premise receipt.
Deleted source evidence invalidates the premise receipt.
Edited canonical claim bytes cannot borrow the old receipt.
Deleted canonical claim removes its authority.
A changed receipt cannot pass its detached HMAC.
A missing receipt confers no authority.
Explicit revocation removes premise authority.
Replacing the key invalidates both old receipts.
A logically supported target still needs unchanged attestation evidence.
An attested target depending on an absent claim is inapplicable.
An applicable attested premise can govern a dependent target.
An expired premise cannot govern the dependent target.
Circular dependencies invalidate source and target governance.
An unresolved contradiction invalidates both otherwise attested premises.
An applicable replacement demotes the old premise.
An attested superseded target cannot be used.
An observed target without a detached receipt remains observed.
A proposed target without a receipt remains proposed.
A supported goal with a deleted target receipt is not admitted.
A supported goal with a tampered target receipt is not admitted.
A receipt alone cannot retain a deleted target's authority.
Deleting irrelevant evidence must not block an independent valid proof.
One remaining valid proof path survives revocation of another.
A step referring to a nonexistent rule is rejected.
A variable binding inconsistent with the premises is rejected.
An unlicensed conclusion cannot borrow a valid step.
An unstated premise cannot be cited by a step.
An incomplete step is not a valid derivation.
A premise established only by a later step is not established yet.
A forged asserted goal cannot change the expected admitted snapshot.
A swapped rule table cannot change the approved rules snapshot.
An artifact for another target cannot satisfy the request.
A valid empty proof does not establish a derived target.
